profile.name: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd (KIMS Hospitals)
profile.founded: Brand began in 2004 with a 300-bed hospital in Secunderabad, Hyderabad (first hospital: Nellore, 2000); founder Dr B. Bhaskara Rao Bollineni, cardio-thoracic surgeon, Chairman & MD; CEO Dr Abhinay Bollineni (his son) since 2019
profile.listing: IPO 16-18 Jun 2021 at ₹825 (₹2,144 cr: fresh issue ₹200 cr, offer for sale ~₹1,944 cr); listed 28-Jun-2021 at a ~22% premium. Shares split 1:5 (face value ₹10 → ₹2), record date 13-Sep-2024
profile.network: Bed capacity 7,459 and 5,639 operational beds in five states (Q1FY27, excluding hospitals run for a fee); 26 hospitals; 'overall bed capacity of 9,600+' including O&M hospitals and planned projects
profile.model: Multi-specialty tertiary hospitals (cardiac, neuro, ortho, renal, gastro, oncology, transplants) at 'affordable' prices in tier-1/2 cities; full-time doctors; doctor-partnership subsidiaries (doctors hold equity in ten hospital companies); expansion by greenfield, acquisition and O&M-with-call-option
profile.src: Q1FY27 investor presentation (3-Aug-2026) pp.5-14, 30; AR FY26 note 2.10(a); IPO coverage (Jun-2021)

annualKpiNote: Company definitions: occupancy = occupied beds ÷ operational beds (census + non-census); ARPOB = hospital revenue ÷ occupied bed-days; ARPP = hospital revenue ÷ IP volume; ALOS = bed-days ÷ IP volume. FY24 operational beds (3,503) were on an older basis (occupancy 61.3%), so the FY24→FY25 fall in occupancy is partly definitional. Revenue identity check (Q1FY27): Σ clusters (occupied beds × 91 days × ARPOB) = ₹1,186 cr vs revenue from operations ₹1,180 cr (+0.5%; O&M fees and intercompany eliminations).

accounting.basis: Ind AS, consolidated, one segment. The company's 'EBITDA' includes other income (FY26 ₹828 cr, 21.1% of total income); Screener's operating profit excludes it (₹815 cr, 20.9%). Both are post-Ind AS 116: rent is not deducted (pre-Ind AS EBITDA FY26 ₹785 cr). We use Screener's basis with lease liabilities in net debt.
accounting.doctorFees: Doctors are paid largely as 'consultancy charges' (₹1,007 cr, 25.8% of FY26 revenue, inside other expenses), on top of employee cost (₹682 cr, 17.5%).
accounting.omAccounting: Two kinds of O&M: Kerala's Kannur and Kollam are consolidated as business combinations (KIMS controls them; right-of-use assets ₹186 cr, O&M rights ₹13 cr, contingent consideration ₹56 cr); Sangli, Guntur and Kompally earn a fee ('medical service fees' ₹16.7 cr in FY26) and are outside the bed KPIs. Call options to buy the O&M hospital companies are fair-valued through P&L (−₹3.8 cr FY26, +₹10.8 cr FY25), exercisable from Jan-2027.
accounting.capitalisation: FY26: ₹34 cr of lease interest and ₹21.5 cr of right-of-use depreciation were capitalised into work in progress; this stops as projects open, which is part of why Q1FY27 interest (₹83 cr) and depreciation (₹101 cr) jumped.
accounting.oneOffs: FY25: ₹12 cr land sale in revenue/EBITDA (Q3), ₹10.9 cr gain on asset sale in other income, ₹38 cr one-time eliminations, ₹6.7 cr non-recurring costs (Q4); FY26: exceptional loss ₹11.2 cr (call option ₹3.8 cr, Labour Codes ₹7.4 cr) and a ₹46 cr deferred-tax credit.
accounting.receivables: Receivable days 52 (FY26) vs 28 (FY22); government-scheme receivables were 'a challenge' (CFO, Aug-2026); expected credit loss ₹9.7 cr in FY26.
accounting.minorities: Profit attributable to owners ₹241 cr vs ₹242 cr total in FY26 (minorities' share of profits in Sunshine, Kondapur and Vizag offset by their share of Bengaluru and Nashik losses); ₹30 cr in FY25. Book value of minority interests ₹311 cr (Mar-26).
